content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are small pieces of chicken meat, usually fried or baked, served with a hot sauce. The product is ready‑to‑eat as it is precooked (code 872).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a popular bar and fast‑food snack worldwide.
Hot sauce may be based on chili, habanero, or Tabasco peppers.
Traditionally wings are marinated in spices before cooking to enhance flavor.
The United States hosts an annual "World's Best Chicken Wings" competition.
Wings contain more protein per gram than most other chicken parts.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken meat provides a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6 and B12 support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets when the sauce is sugar‑free.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Wings provide iron, zinc, and phosphorus important for blood and bone health.

items.title: Capsaicin may boost metabolism
items.content: The spicy sauce’s capsaicin can increase metabolic rate and promote satiety.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Hot sauces often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Spicy sauce can irritate the stomach
items.content: Those with gastritis or ulcers should be cautious.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Fried wings can be calorie‑rich due to oil and sauce.

items.title: Risk of bacterial growth if stored improperly
items.content: Keeping the product above 4 °C for more than 2 hours increases the risk of contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are eaten hot as a snack, served with extra sauce, coleslaw, or celery sticks. Their hand‑held nature makes them popular at parties and sporting events.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the ready‑to‑eat product in the refrigerator at +4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container at -18 °C for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of ≥ 75 °C before consumption.
